action_items.item: Fix the division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, working out which input produces a zero divisor. Add a regression test for it before monthly-spend-feature is enabled again.
Require progressive rollout for feature flags that change account page behavior, with automatic rollback when the error rate of the affected path rises.
Alert on the account page error rate over a shorter window, or on a rise in ZeroDivisionError log lines, so that paging comes sooner after onset.
Make flag toggle events in the change feed carry the time the flag took effect, and let the Investigator search flag changes as well as deploys. Check why the toggle was timestamped after the onset.

Before an incident is resolved by hand, require the post-revert recovery check to finish, or have the resolver record that recovery was verified. Treat a withdrawn mitigation as an open question about cause.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers loading the io-shop account page got errors. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, and the HighErrorRate alert fired.
The failing account page requests were raising ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors began at the onset of the rise in error rate.

That code runs only when monthly-spend-feature is on. Flag evaluations were nearly all off at first, with a small share on just before the onset. They were all on from the onset onward, which matches the start of the errors.

An admin switched monthly-spend-feature on, and it took effect for all traffic within about a minute, with no staged rollout or error-based stop. The change feed timestamp for this toggle is slightly later than the onset, so the exact toggle time is uncertain.
The spend summary code does not handle the case where its divisor is zero. The record does not show which input is zero or why the code was not tested for it, so the chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went to all traffic almost at once, with no staged rollout or automatic rollback on error rate, so a code bug hit every account page request.
The spend summary code had no guard or test for a zero divisor before the flag was enabled in production.
Detection was slow. The alert was raised several minutes after the errors began, so most of the impact had passed before Argus started.
The change feed gave a flag toggle timestamp later than the onset, and the Investigator's search of production changes returned nothing. Responders could not easily tie the errors to the toggle.

The incident was resolved by a person while Argus's check of the revert was still waiting and showed the service not at baseline. The revert was then judged withdrawn, so recovery was never confirmed as caused by the flag being off.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, a large share of shoppers loading their account page got an error. The error rate was {errors_while_broken} on average, against {errors_before} beforehand, so about {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have. It peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The cause was a new feature, the monthly spend summary, being turned on for everyone. It contains a calculation bug that crashes the page. Argus turned the feature off and a person kept it off and paged the checkout team. The metrics show recovery at {recovered}. However, Argus's own last checks still showed the service not back at baseline, so the record does not confirm that turning the feature off was what ended the errors. The calculation bug is not yet fixed.

got_lucky: The failure was limited to the account page code path behind one flag, so turning the flag off was a cheap and safe action. It could have been much worse if the bug sat on an unflagged path.
went_well: Argus took the alert up within seconds and read metrics, changes and logs in one pass. It named the flag and the ZeroDivisionError as the leading cause in a few seconds.
The flag was turned off quickly and a person kept it off and paged the checkout team.
went_wrong: The revert was judged withdrawn with the service still not at baseline, so the record does not show that it fixed the incident.
The incident was resolved by hand before the check finished.
The alert came well after the errors began, and the change feed did not show the flag toggle at the time of the Investigator's search.

input.root_cause: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on for account page traffic, and the code path it enables divides by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. Every request that hit that line failed, and nothing staged the rollout or stopped it when errors rose. Why the divisor is zero is not shown in the record.
